coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop)
names: Union Iron Works Foundry and Warehouse
record.summary: The oldest surviving shipyard buildings at Pier 70: the 1885-86 brick Machine Shop and blacksmith/boiler shop (113/114, joined by a 1914 concrete connector, 492 ft long) and the 1916-17 reinforced-concrete foundry and warehouse (115/116) beside it. Closed and red-tagged in 2001, they were rehabilitated by Orton Development with a buckling-restrained-brace steel system and public atrium, receiving certificates of occupancy in November 2017 (115/116) and April 2018 (113/114), and were subleased to Uber Advanced Technologies Group and Gusto.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprints -- high confidence in each piece's outline and in the group's overall position (confirmed to sit within Figure 6.4.2's own '113-116' box). Individual identification of which piece(s) correspond to Building 113 vs 114 vs 115 vs 116 specifically is NOT possible from the sources checked -- Figure 6.4.2 draws them as one undifferentiated box, and the 2013 HPC packet's textual description ('115 and 116 abut Building 113/114') does not give a precise position. Rather than guess, this feature represents the combined complex, consistent with how it is actually shown in the source diagram. The combined footprint here (~9751 sq m / ~104,957 sqft) is larger than Building 113/114 alone (~86,100 sqft per its documented 492ft x 175ft footprint) and smaller than 113/114 + 115/116's combined documented GSF (~95,000 + ~38,000 = ~133,000 GSF) -- broadly consistent given GSF can include multi-level floor area not captured by a footprint, but not independently verified piece-by-piece.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4111004) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups Buildings 113/114 and 115/116 into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprints instead, matched to the specific area of the lot that Figure 6.4.2 itself draws as the historic '113-116' complex.
notes.regulatory_context: Union Iron Works Machine Shop and Foundry, Buildings 113/114, on the south side of 20th Street just east of Illinois Street -- 'one of the most valuable and most vulnerable historic resources on the site' per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E). Two unreinforced brick structures (Machine Shop, built 1885, and Foundry, built 1886) joined in 1914 by a reinforced concrete connector; building-length skylights, rows of high arched windows; ~95,000 GSF, 492ft long by 175ft wide, ~62ft tall. Buildings 115 and 116 abut Building 113/114, constructed 1916-1917, ~38,000 GSF, 57ft tall, with 'unusual windows and monitor skylights.' At review time the complex was red-tagged and subject to an engineer's advisory of imminent collapse. Rehab by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) included demolition/relocation of later metal additions on the west and south facades, a new steel seismic system tied into the brick perimeter, and demolition of two minor eastern appendages (Buildings 23/24, ~1,500 GSF). Proposed for industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail, alongside Building 14, framing a shared ~45,000 sf courtyard.

Dr. D. E. Melliss, civil engineer (113/114); designer of 115/116 not recorded
113/114: 492 ft by 175 ft 6 in by 62 ft tall; 115/116: 218 ft by 174 ft by 57 ft 2 in
113/114: 89,686 (NRHP), 95,157 before and 129,228 after rehabilitation (Port); 115/116: 33,858 (NRHP), 38,694 before and 53,625 after (Port)

New perimeter steel framing at two levels stabilizes the unreinforced brick walls (up to 18 inches out of plumb); buckling-restrained braced frames provide lateral resistance; new interior steel frame and mezzanines
Office and PDR (113/114); PDR (115/116); 'New American Workplace' light-industrial definition with ancillary office, showroom and retail
Uber Advanced Technologies Group (113 West, 114, 115, 116) and Gusto (113 East) per the Port's January 2019 sublease list; STRUCTURE later describes 'two technology tenants'
Building 113-114 atrium (the 1914 connector) and the ~45,000 sq ft plaza framed with Building 14 are publicly accessible under Master Lease Exhibit K
Later additions Buildings 23 and 24 on the east end (1941 shed and washroom, ~1,500 gsf) removed to facilitate rehabilitation

Built as the Union Iron Works' machine, blacksmith and boiler shops; the Building 115 foundry produced over a million pounds of castings a month by 1919; 'Pacific Coast Steel Corporation' lettering survives on 115/116
